questions.subject: Programming skills · Sequencing
questions.text: A parcel kiosk must print a label before attaching it. Which pair preserves that dependency?
questions.explanation: The label must exist before it can be attached.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Sequencing
questions.text: A program sets lamp = off, then lamp = on. What is the final state?
questions.explanation: The later assignment replaces the earlier lamp value.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Sequencing
questions.text: An app saves a receipt before calculating its total. Which change fixes the order?
answers: Calculate the total before saving the receipt
questions.explanation: The saved receipt should use the completed calculation.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Sequencing
questions.text: Why write a numbered plan for a parcel-sorting program?
answers: To specify the order of its actions
To guarantee that no tests are needed
questions.explanation: A numbered plan makes action dependencies explicit.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Debugging
questions.text: A thermostat should turn on below 18 degrees but turns on at 24. What is useful evidence?
answers: The measured value and the comparison result
questions.explanation: The temperature and comparison reveal why the branch runs.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Debugging
questions.text: An order contains two items but its total includes only one. What should be traced?
answers: Which items reach the total calculation
questions.explanation: Tracing item processing can reveal a skipped calculation.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Debugging
questions.text: Why keep a failing input when repairing a program?
answers: To rerun the same case after the fix
To prove every other input fails
questions.explanation: A repeatable case lets you compare behavior before and after a change.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Debugging
questions.text: After changing one calculation, what should a developer do?
answers: Test the failing case and related working cases
questions.explanation: The fix should solve the failure without breaking related behavior.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Sequencing
questions.text: A timer waits 2 seconds, rings, waits 3 seconds, then flashes. When does the flash occur after starting?
questions.explanation: The two sequential waits add to 5 seconds.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Sequencing
questions.text: Two tasks must run in order: unlock a cabinet, then open it. Why is order important?
answers: Both tasks must have equal duration
Opening depends on the cabinet already being unlocked
The shorter task must always be first
questions.explanation: A dependency requires one task to finish before the next can succeed.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Sequencing
questions.text: A display shows Red, then Blue, then Green. Swapping the first two commands produces what order?
questions.explanation: Only the first two positions are exchanged.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Sequencing
questions.text: A recipe app skips its timer step. Which comparison best helps locate the omission?
answers: The phone's brand against its name
The intended steps against the executed steps
questions.explanation: Comparing planned and executed actions reveals missing steps.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Graphics
questions.text: On a coordinate plane where x increases rightward, a marker moves from x = 12 to x = 19. How far right did it move?
questions.explanation: The change is 19 minus 12, or 7.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Graphics
questions.text: A drawing tool faces east and turns 90 degrees counterclockwise. Which direction does it face?
questions.explanation: A counterclockwise quarter-turn from east points north.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Graphics
questions.text: A pen draws a line of length 15, then one of length 25 without turning. What is the combined length?
questions.explanation: Consecutive straight segments add: 15 + 25 = 40.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Graphics
questions.text: Which action moves a cursor without leaving a drawn line in a pen-based drawing tool?
questions.explanation: A lifted pen changes position without marking the surface.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Sprites
questions.text: A game icon stays at the same coordinates but changes from gray to green. Which property changed?
questions.explanation: Its visible styling changed while its location stayed fixed.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Sprites
questions.text: Two screen objects use the same picture but occupy different positions. Are they necessarily the same object?
answers: Yes; an image can be used only once
Yes; position does not belong to objects
No; shared pictures cannot be displayed
No; separate objects can share an image
questions.explanation: Objects can have independent state while reusing one visual resource.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Sprites
questions.text: A character has x, y, and health values. What do those values describe?
questions.explanation: State records information about an object at a particular moment.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Sprites
questions.text: Which change makes a map marker larger without moving its center?
answers: Increase its scale while keeping its position
questions.explanation: Scale controls size independently of the center coordinates.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Sprites
questions.text: Code tries to move an object named beacon before creating it. What is missing?
questions.explanation: A program needs a valid object before it can operate on that object.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Sprites
questions.text: Three markers share a class, but only marker B should blink. What must the command identify?
questions.explanation: A specific target prevents unintended changes to the other markers.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Sprites
questions.text: Two objects both start with health 10. Object A loses 3 health. If their state is independent, what is B's health?
questions.explanation: Changing A's independent health value does not change B's value.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Sprites
questions.text: Why give screen objects meaningful names such as exitMarker?
answers: To make the intended target easier to recognize
To make the program execute faster automatically
questions.explanation: Clear names help a reader understand which object code controls.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Design
questions.text: A museum kiosk needs to explain three exhibits. Which plan is easiest to test?
answers: One labeled button for each exhibit
Three unlabeled buttons with changing meanings
questions.explanation: Explicit labels and responses give each interaction an observable purpose.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Design
questions.text: A project explains how weather sensors help gardeners. Which feature supports that purpose?
answers: A reading display linked to a watering recommendation
A hidden score with no explanation
questions.explanation: The feature connects the displayed measurement to its practical use.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Design
questions.text: What should a tester know before checking an interaction?
answers: The input to try and the expected response
The number of files on the device
questions.explanation: A test compares a specified action with an expected result.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Design
questions.text: A visitor cannot find the reset control. Which revision addresses the feedback?
answers: Add a visible control labeled Reset
questions.explanation: A visible descriptive control makes the action discoverable.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Events
questions.text: A map should zoom when the plus button is clicked. Which event should trigger zooming?
answers: A click on the plus button
questions.explanation: The handler should respond to the specified user action.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Events
questions.text: Pressing R should reset a timer. Where should the reset action be placed?
answers: Only in an unrelated click handler
questions.explanation: The matching key event should execute the reset action.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Events
questions.text: A button click runs two handlers, and both add 1 to a counter. How much is added per click?
questions.explanation: Each handler contributes one increment when that click triggers both.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Events
questions.text: Why test a button with both mouse and keyboard activation when both are supported?
answers: To ensure every event fires twice
To verify both input routes perform the intended action
questions.explanation: Different supported inputs should produce the intended equivalent response.

questions.subject: Programming skills · State
questions.text: A digital greenhouse has a water button. Which state change could represent watering?
questions.explanation: A moisture value models a relevant part of the simulation.

questions.subject: Programming skills · State
questions.text: A cart keeps moving after Pause is clicked. What should be inspected?
answers: Whether its movement update is still enabled
questions.explanation: Pausing must stop or disable the code that advances movement.

questions.subject: Programming skills · State
questions.text: A simulation restarts. Which action makes its starting behavior predictable?
answers: Randomize every value without a rule
Initialize its state to documented starting values
Keep arbitrary values from an old run
questions.explanation: Known initial values make behavior repeatable and testable.

questions.subject: Programming skills · State
questions.text: A visitor clicks Start twice. Which rule prevents two concurrent timers?
answers: Ignore Start while a timer is already running
Create another timer on every click
Delete Pause after the first click
questions.explanation: A running-state check prevents duplicate timer creation.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Events
questions.text: A reminder is scheduled for 8 seconds after Start. What triggers its handler?
answers: The timer reaching the scheduled delay
questions.explanation: The timer event is tied to elapsed time after scheduling.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Events
questions.text: An animation updates every 0.5 seconds. How many updates occur at 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0 seconds?
questions.explanation: The four listed update times each cause one update.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Events
questions.text: A scheduled warning should not appear after Cancel. What should Cancel do?
questions.explanation: Removing the pending timer prevents that delayed action from firing.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Events
questions.text: Why avoid assuming that a browser timer fires at an exact real-world instant?
answers: Other work can delay the callback
The user's name determines the delay
questions.explanation: Busy execution can postpone a scheduled callback.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Events
questions.text: A weather app displays details immediately instead of waiting for More. Which placement is suspect?
answers: The details action is in startup code rather than the More handler
The button label uses a capital letter
questions.explanation: Startup code runs without waiting for that button event.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Events
questions.text: Two buttons should open different panels. What test checks their routing?
answers: Activate each button and verify its own panel
Click one button and assume the other works
questions.explanation: Each input-to-response mapping needs its own check.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Events
questions.text: An alarm handler should update the label and play a tone. What must its code include?
answers: Only a comment naming the tone
questions.explanation: The event response must execute both requested operations.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Events
questions.text: Why keep an event handler focused on a clear action?
answers: It makes all other handlers unnecessary
It changes every variable into a constant
Its input and outcome are easier to understand and test
questions.explanation: A focused responsibility makes behavior easier to reason about.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: A loop prints one ticket per iteration and repeats 7 times. How many tickets are printed?
questions.explanation: One print per iteration across seven iterations produces seven tickets.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: A badge must be shown once after a loop ends. Where does the display command belong?
answers: In a comment before the loop
questions.explanation: An action after the loop runs once after repetition finishes.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: Which task naturally fits a repeat-8 loop?
answers: Repeat until a user supplies an unknown password
Wait for an unpredictable network reply
Apply the same stamp eight times
questions.explanation: The stamp task has a known repetition count.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: A loop contains two moves and runs 5 times. How many move commands execute?
questions.explanation: Two moves per iteration times five iterations equals ten.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: A display needs six identical cards followed by one footer. Which plan fits?
answers: Repeat the card six times, then draw the footer
Repeat the footer six times, then one card
Draw the footer inside each card
Draw one card and omit the footer
questions.explanation: Only the repeated card belongs inside the six-iteration loop.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: A setup command should run once before processing 9 records. Where should it go?
answers: At the end of every iteration
Only in the ninth record's data
questions.explanation: Setup outside the loop avoids repeating initialization.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: A loop starts a subtotal at zero on every iteration. Why can that lose earlier additions?
answers: Each iteration overwrites the accumulated subtotal
questions.explanation: Resetting the accumulator discards the previous running value.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: A printer repeats four batches of three labels. How many labels are produced?
questions.explanation: Four groups of three labels give twelve labels.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: A tray has 4 rows with 5 slots in each row. An outer loop visits rows and an inner loop visits slots. How many slots are visited?
questions.explanation: The inner five visits repeat for each of four rows.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: What distinguishes a nested loop from two consecutive loops?
answers: One loop executes inside another loop's body
Both loops must have the same count
questions.explanation: Nesting places the inner repetition within each outer iteration.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: An outer loop runs 2 times and an inner loop runs 6 times per outer iteration. How many inner iterations occur?
questions.explanation: Each of the two outer iterations includes six inner iterations.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: An inner loop should restart for each new row. When should its starting value be set?
answers: At the start of each row's inner loop
questions.explanation: Each row needs a fresh traversal of its columns.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Graphics
questions.text: A circular dial has 8 equally spaced marks. What angle separates neighboring marks?
questions.explanation: A full turn of 360 degrees divided by eight gives 45 degrees.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Graphics
questions.text: A repeating tile has 3 drawn edges and is placed 7 times. How many edge draws occur?
questions.explanation: Three edge draws for each of seven placements gives twenty-one.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Graphics
questions.text: To double a regular polygon's size without changing its shape, what should change?
answers: Double all side lengths and keep its turn angles
questions.explanation: Uniformly scaling lengths preserves the shape's angles.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Graphics
questions.text: A pattern rotates 120 degrees after each placement. How many such turns make one full turn?
questions.explanation: Three turns of 120 degrees total 360 degrees.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Conditionals
questions.text: A door opens if badgeValid is true. When should it remain closed?
answers: Only when the variable name is short
questions.explanation: The stated rule grants entry only when the Boolean test is true.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Conditionals
questions.text: Which expression tests whether a numeric temperature is below 5?
questions.explanation: A less-than comparison produces the required true-or-false result.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Conditionals
questions.text: A delivery robot checks for a barrier before each move. Why repeat the check?
answers: The first check changes every future position
Conditions can be used only once
The next position may have a different barrier state
questions.explanation: The decision should use information relevant to the next movement.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Conditionals
questions.text: An alert should appear only when battery < 15. Which test case checks the false outcome?
questions.explanation: Forty is not less than fifteen, so the alert condition is false.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Conditionals
questions.text: If parcelWeight > 5, use the large bin; otherwise use the small bin. Which bin gets weight 5?
questions.explanation: Five does not satisfy the strictly-greater-than-five test.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Conditionals
questions.text: In an ordinary if/else, how are the two branches selected?
answers: Only the else branch can execute
questions.explanation: True selects the if branch and false selects the else branch.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Conditionals
questions.text: If member is true, price = 8; else price = 11. What is the price for a nonmember?
questions.explanation: A nonmember makes member false, selecting the else assignment.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Conditionals
questions.text: Which pair best tests both branches of age >= 13?
questions.explanation: Twelve is false and thirteen is true, including the decision boundary.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: While supplies > 0, remove one supply. Starting with supplies = 4, how many iterations run?
questions.explanation: Four removals reduce the value to zero, where the condition becomes false.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: A pre-test while loop checks ready == false. If ready is already true, how many iterations run?
questions.explanation: The condition is false before the first iteration.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: While count < 3, print count and increase it by 1. Starting at count = 1, what is printed?
questions.explanation: Values one and two satisfy the condition; three does not.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: A loop waits while jobsRemaining > 0 but never changes jobsRemaining. What is a concern?
answers: It must stop after one iteration
questions.explanation: The condition may remain true if nothing changes the relevant state.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Conditionals
questions.text: A warning appears when speed > 30. Which value tests the boundary without triggering it?
questions.explanation: Thirty equals the boundary and does not satisfy a strict greater-than test.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Conditionals
questions.text: A cooler runs if hot AND powerAvailable. Which case keeps it off?
answers: powerAvailable is true and hot is true
hot is true and powerAvailable is false
hot is true and powerAvailable is true
questions.explanation: An AND expression requires both parts to be true.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Conditionals
questions.text: An access check accepts badge OR supervisorApproval. Which case is accepted?
answers: No badge, but supervisorApproval is true
questions.explanation: An OR expression is true when at least one part is true.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Conditionals
questions.text: A sensor program handles low, normal, and high values. Which test plan is strongest?
answers: Test only the largest possible value
Test at least one value in each range and the boundaries
questions.explanation: Different ranges and boundaries can expose different decision errors.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: A pre-test loop repeats while the destination has not been reached. What makes it stop?
answers: The loop count is always two
questions.explanation: Once the destination is reached, the while condition becomes false.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: A process handles one queued item per iteration until the queue is empty. It starts with 6 items and receives no new items. How many iterations are needed?
questions.explanation: Each iteration removes one of the six starting items.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: Why must a repeat-until rule specify when its condition is checked?
answers: A condition cannot be checked twice
All languages use identical loop semantics
Checking before or after the body can change the first iteration
questions.explanation: Pre-test and post-test loops can behave differently when the condition starts true.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Loops
questions.text: A loop should stop when remaining <= 0. Why is that safer than remaining == 0 if updates may subtract 2?
answers: It forces the value to stay positive
It also stops when the value skips below zero
questions.explanation: A decrement of two can pass from one to minus one without equaling zero.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Conditionals
questions.text: A sorter checks red first, blue second, and otherwise uses a mixed bin. Where does a yellow item go?
questions.explanation: Yellow matches neither named color, so the fallback branch runs.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Conditionals
questions.text: What is a nested conditional?
answers: A variable whose name has two words
A decision inside another decision's branch
questions.explanation: A branch can contain another condition to refine a decision.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Conditionals
questions.text: A program first checks whether a file exists, then checks its size inside that branch. When is size checked?
answers: Only when the file-exists branch runs
questions.explanation: The inner decision is reached through its containing branch.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Conditionals
questions.text: If score >= 90 use Gold; else if score >= 70 use Silver; else Bronze. What label does 85 receive?
questions.explanation: Eighty-five fails the first test and satisfies the second.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Functions
questions.text: A function named sendReceipt groups the steps for sending one receipt. What does calling it do?
answers: Run every function in the app
questions.explanation: A call invokes the function's behavior.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Functions
questions.text: A packBox function adds 2 inserts per call. Five calls add how many inserts?
questions.explanation: Two inserts per call times five calls gives ten.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Functions
questions.text: A function is defined but never called, and no event invokes it. Will its body run just because it is defined?
answers: Only if its name is long
questions.explanation: Defining behavior does not by itself invoke that behavior.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Functions
questions.text: Which function name best describes checking an entered postal code?
questions.explanation: The name identifies the task rather than an unrelated detail.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Functions
questions.text: A function doubleValue(n) returns n * 2. What does doubleValue(9) return?
questions.explanation: The parameter receives nine and multiplication produces eighteen.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Functions
questions.text: What is the role of a parameter?
answers: Receive an input value for a function call
Always store the final screen image
questions.explanation: Parameters let the same function work with supplied inputs.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Functions
questions.text: A function returns a calculated shipping fee. How can its caller use that result?
answers: Store it or include it in another calculation
Assume it has been printed automatically
questions.explanation: Returning supplies a result to the calling code; display is a separate action.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Functions
questions.text: Why test a calculation function with several inputs?
answers: To guarantee every possible program is correct
To remove its need for inputs
To check its rule beyond a single example
questions.explanation: Different cases can reveal limits or mistakes hidden by one example.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Functions
questions.text: Several screens use the same price-formatting rule. Where should that shared rule live?
answers: In a variable name with no code
In separately edited copies on every screen
questions.explanation: Centralizing the rule makes consistent updates easier.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Functions
questions.text: A shared function formats prices incorrectly. Where should the common mistake be repaired?
questions.explanation: Repairing the shared behavior affects the calls that use it.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Functions
questions.text: Which task is a clear function-sized responsibility?
answers: Do every possible task in the app
Calculate the tax for one subtotal
questions.explanation: A focused responsibility has a clear input, purpose, and result.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Functions
questions.text: After changing a shared function, which tests matter?
answers: No tests if it still has the same name
Its own cases and the features that call it
Only a screenshot of its name
questions.explanation: A change can affect both the function and its callers.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Variables
questions.text: A form asks for a display name. What does the user's typed response provide?
questions.explanation: A form collects information supplied by its user.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Variables
questions.text: name stores Imani. The program joins Welcome, a space, and name. What text results?
questions.explanation: The stored value is inserted after the greeting and space.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Variables
questions.text: Why validate an entered quantity before using it in arithmetic?
answers: Only negative numbers can be typed
The input might be empty or nonnumeric
Every input is already a number
questions.explanation: User input must meet the calculation's required format and range.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Variables
questions.text: A user enters 7 as text. What may be needed before numeric addition?
answers: Convert and validate it as a number
Add quotation marks around every number
questions.explanation: Text and numeric values can behave differently during addition.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Variables
questions.text: A counter starts at 3 and increases by 2 after each of four scans. What is its final value?
questions.explanation: The initial three plus four increments of two equals eleven.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Variables
questions.text: Where should a session's score usually be initialized if it should survive multiple clicks?
answers: Only after each point is displayed
At session start, outside the scoring click handler
At the start of every scoring click
questions.explanation: Repeated initialization would erase the accumulated score.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Variables
questions.text: A counter has value 8. The statement counter = counter - 3 leaves what value?
questions.explanation: The updated value is eight minus three.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Variables
questions.text: Which variable name best describes the number of completed deliveries?
questions.explanation: The name communicates what quantity is stored.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Variables
questions.text: width starts at 12. Before each of three drawings it increases by 4. What widths are drawn?
questions.explanation: The update happens before each draw, so the first width is sixteen.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Variables
questions.text: A diagram uses the same margin variable on all four sides. What does changing that variable support?
answers: A guarantee that every screen fits
questions.explanation: A shared value can control repeated dimensions consistently.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Variables
questions.text: radius is assigned 6, then assigned 9 before drawing a circle. Which radius does the drawing use?
questions.explanation: The most recent assignment is nine.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Variables
questions.text: Why record a dimension's unit in its description or name?
answers: To remove every need for scaling
To force every image to be square
To avoid mixing quantities such as pixels and millimeters
questions.explanation: Explicit units prevent incompatible measurements from being confused.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Variables
questions.text: A basket starts with 2 parts. Deliveries add 4, then 3 more. What is the final count?
questions.explanation: The running total is 2 + 4 + 3 = 9.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Variables
questions.text: A display shows yesterday's stock after a new delivery. What should be checked?
answers: Whether the stored stock and display were updated
questions.explanation: Both the data update and the presentation may need to run.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Variables
questions.text: A total begins at 0 and adds each value in [2, 5, 1]. What does it become?
questions.explanation: Accumulation adds all three values: 2 + 5 + 1.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Variables
questions.text: Which operation records one additional completed task?
questions.explanation: An increment increases the existing count by one.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Counting loops
questions.text: A counting loop uses 2, 4, 6, and 8. What is its step?
questions.explanation: Each successive value increases by two.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Counting loops
questions.text: A loop includes every integer from 3 through 7. How many iterations run?
questions.explanation: The included values are 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Counting loops
questions.text: Which three choices describe a numeric counting range?
answers: Starting value, stopping rule, and step
questions.explanation: These choices determine the counter values and when counting stops.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Counting loops
questions.text: A loop starts at 10 and subtracts 2 while the value is at least 4. Which values are used?
questions.explanation: Four is included by the at-least-four stopping rule; two is not.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Counting loops
questions.text: A pattern uses sizes 6, 12, 18, and 24. What is the increment?
questions.explanation: The difference between neighboring sizes is six.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Counting loops
questions.text: A counter takes 1, 2, 3. Each iteration draws a bar of length counter * 5. What lengths result?
questions.explanation: Multiplying each counter value by five yields the three lengths.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Counting loops
questions.text: A loop starts at 0, continues while i < 4, and adds 1 each time. Which value is never used in its body?
questions.explanation: The body runs for zero through three; the test fails at four.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Counting loops
questions.text: A pattern needs exactly five bars but produces six. What should be checked first?
answers: Whether the loop's bounds include an extra value
questions.explanation: An inclusive bound can create an extra iteration.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Design
questions.text: A class plans an accessible homework reminder. What should be specified first?
answers: The color of an unused icon
Who will use it and which task it must support
questions.explanation: Purpose and users guide meaningful feature decisions.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Design
questions.text: Only one day remains before a demo. Which choice best protects a useful result?
answers: Finish and test the essential reminder flow first
questions.explanation: A reliable core feature provides value before optional polish.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Design
questions.text: A tester reports that saving fails only with an empty title. What should the developer capture?
answers: Steps, input values, expected result, and actual result
Only a screenshot of the desktop wallpaper
questions.explanation: A clear report makes the failure reproducible.

questions.subject: Programming skills · Design
questions.text: Which reflection gives actionable information for the next version?
answers: Everything is perfect because we finished
There is nothing left to test
The project title has enough letters
Users missed Reset, so we will test a clearer label and placement
questions.explanation: Specific observations can lead to a testable improvement.
